A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study despite revised terminology and presentation. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original VTAB-1K comparisons, ensemble analyses, many-shot experiments, and CLIP distribution-shift evaluations.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds augmentation tests, DINOv2 comparisons, and within-family prediction-overlap results.

M1.justification: The PEFT methods and WiSE procedures are retained. However, v1 specifies averaging logits for prediction ensembles, whereas v4 Section 4 and Figure 4 specify majority voting while Appendix C still specifies averaging logits. This contradiction prevents establishing whether the ensemble procedure actually changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 19 VTAB tasks, full-data CIFAR-100/RESISC/Clevr-Distance, and ImageNet with four distribution shifts. The added augmentation and backbone comparisons reuse existing tasks rather than introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding main experiments retain the same tuning methods and baselines. V4's stated increase from 13 to 14 PEFT methods includes VPT-Shallow, already evaluated in v1 Table 1. DINOv2 supplies an additional backbone setting rather than a new tuning-method competitor.

E3.justification: V4 adds substantial experimental controls: augmentation versus no augmentation on nine tasks (Table 4), and DINOv2 versus ImageNet-21K initialization on twelve tasks (Table 7). Existing principal splits, budgets, and tuning grids remain. The mentioned ViT-L/ViT-H results are not actually presented and are not counted.

E4.justification: New analyses test augmentation sensitivity, illustrate task-damaging transformations on KITTI, examine prediction overlap within versus across PEFT families, and investigate dependence on pre-training through DINOv2. These substantially extend v1's existing drop-path, parameter-size, prediction-diversity, and WiSE analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain Table 1's across-method relative standard deviations. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the additional results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds augmentation scores, within-family overlap counts, and DINOv2 results. For example, Table 7 reports Houl. Adapter accuracy of 22.1 on Caltech101 with DINOv2 versus 92.1 with IN21k, under different backbone conditions. Table 1 is numerically unchanged, but Table 2 revises Houl. Adapter's distribution-shift average from 56.12 to 56.9.

T1.justification: The existing ViT and PEFT equations are retained, with no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision. Added CLIP scoring notation explains the previously described classification setup.

C1.justification: The central claims about tuned accuracy, complementary predictions, many-shot effectiveness, and WiSE robustness remain. V4 additionally claims priority for studying WiSE with PEFT and explicitly presents a reproducible evaluation framework as a contribution.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of DINOv2-dependent failures, including a sequential-versus-parallel adapter hypothesis, and explains how augmentation can undermine task requirements. It also adds feature-ensemble and loss-basin explanations for WiSE. Section 6 newly qualifies its account of PEFT's success as non-definitive.

D1.justification: V4 newly discloses using 80 CLIP prompts for classifier initialization and names the augmentation transforms, while retaining the main tuning grids, budgets, and hardware information. It updates the repository pointer but omits v1's explicit 224-by-224 resizing and low-shot normalization instructions.

R1.justification: V4 adds references including V-PETL Bench, DINOv2, Git Re-Basin, and task arithmetic, while removing several peripheral citations. It softens v1's claim of comparing more methods than prior studies and adds WiSE-for-PEFT priority language, without fundamentally changing its research positioning.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and condensed, PETL terminology and the title become PEFT, and an explicit contributions paragraph is added. Appendix subsections are reorganized, the computational-scope limitation moves there, and extensive figure-reading explanations are added.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column layout and substantially rearranges displays: an existing Venn diagram moves into Figure 1, prediction plots are merged, and the four-panel interpretation figure is reorganized. New augmentation and DINOv2 tables, dataset illustrations, and within-family Venn diagrams are added; captions and robustness-axis labels are revised.

improvement.justification: The augmentation controls, DINOv2 comparison, and within-family overlap analysis strengthen the practical evidence and expose dependencies absent from v1. These useful additions improve an already extensive study, but conflicting ensemble descriptions, omitted preprocessing details, and insufficiently documented DINOv2 settings limit the overall gain.
